ground_truth: EXACT BY CONSTRUCTION — the diff in source/changes.diff was authored for this task, so every fact below is checkable against it without judgement. Match on substance, not wording: a fact counts as recalled if any of its synonyms (or an obvious paraphrase) appears and the claim is not contradicted elsewhere in the answer.

key_points.point: Four existing files are modified and no file is added, deleted or renamed: src/ingest/config.py, src/ingest/normalize.py, src/ingest/reader.py, tests/test_normalize.py.
synonyms: three modules under src/ingest plus one test file

key_points.point: BREAKING: the retry setting is renamed from retry_limit to max_retries on both the IngestConfig dataclass field and the load_config() keyword argument, with no alias, property or deprecation shim — code reading config.retry_limit or calling load_config(retry_limit=...) now fails.
synonyms: attribute/keyword rename with no backwards compatibility

key_points.point: BREAKING AND SILENT: load_config now reads the JSON key "max_retries" instead of "retry_limit" with no fallback, so an existing config file that still says retry_limit does not error — the key is ignored and the default is used instead.
synonyms: old config files silently fall back to the default
existing config files must be updated

key_points.point: The default retry count changes from 3 to 5 (both the dataclass default and the load_config keyword default).

BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: parse_timestamp now treats a timestamp with no UTC offset as UTC (tzinfo replaced with timezone.utc) instead of the machine's local timezone (datetime.astimezone()), so naive timestamps are no longer shifted by the reader's local offset.
synonyms: naive timestamps are now interpreted as UTC
offset-less timestamps assumed UTC instead of local time
removes a timezone shift that depended on the machine running the ingest

key_points.point: BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: normalize_rows no longer aborts the whole batch on the first bad row. It gains a keyword-only on_error parameter defaulting to "skip", which drops unnormalizable rows and logs a warning with the skipped count; on_error="raise" restores the old abort behaviour.
synonyms: bad rows are skipped by default instead of raising
new on_error argument, defaults to skip
partial results instead of an exception
logs how many rows were skipped

key_points.point: The read_batch implementation is moved to a private _read_batch_impl, but the public name is preserved by the module-level alias read_batch = _read_batch_impl, so the public API and signature are unchanged and callers importing read_batch are NOT affected.
synonyms: renamed internally but the public name still works
not a breaking change because the alias preserves it

key_points.point: read_all is updated to the renamed setting (config.max_retries) and calls _read_batch_impl directly.

The tests are updated to the new behaviour: test_parse_timestamp_naive_is_local becomes test_parse_timestamp_naive_is_utc, and the abort-on-bad-row test is replaced by three tests covering skip-by-default, on_error="raise", and rejection of an unknown on_error value (net: two more tests).
synonyms: tests updated for the UTC assumption
new tests for the skip/raise modes
test coverage added for on_error validation

key_points.point: normalize_rows validates on_error and raises ValueError for any value other than "skip" or "raise".

anti_facts.claim: Calling the read_batch -> _read_batch_impl rename a breaking change / an API removal.
synonyms: read_batch was renamed, update your imports
anti_facts.why: The diff adds `read_batch = _read_batch_impl` immediately after the function, so the public name and signature survive. This is the deliberate looks-breaking-but-is-not change; asserting it is breaking is a false positive and must cost precision.

anti_facts.claim: Calling normalize_rows' new on_error parameter a breaking signature change.
synonyms: normalize_rows signature changed, callers must update
anti_facts.why: on_error is keyword-only with a default, so every existing call still type-checks and runs. The DEFAULT BEHAVIOUR change (kf6) is real and must be reported; an API break is not.

anti_facts.claim: Any invented content: a migration script, a CHANGELOG entry, a version bump, new files or modules, an issue/ticket number, a performance claim, or a deprecation warning being emitted.
anti_facts.why: None of it is in the diff. Long prose invites confabulation; this is the axis that catches it.

notes: Recall = key_points found / 10, weighting 'high' above 'medium' above 'low'. Precision penalty = anti_facts asserted. kf7 vs af1 is the discriminator the task exists for: one genuine breaking change (kf2/kf3) and one change that looks breaking but is not (kf7). A model that reports both as breaking has pattern-matched on 'rename' rather than read the diff. Scoring is offline (Opus, Stage 3); this file is not consumed by an automated grader.
